startup.name: Wayco
startup.description: Wayco is building a unified data intelligence layer for medical treatment of legal cases. From the first intake to instant settlement.

yc_acceptance.basis: Test note: this company was accepted to YC, so this is only the forward estimate. Starting prior is about 1 percent for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent third party range, per references/yc_acceptance.md). Vertical legal and medical AI with a five person team (larger than typical, up), a defined paying buyer in plaintiff law firms (up), strong market timing from funded legal AI categories (up), but a crowded space (down). Net about 2 percent.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most likely say the medical legal records space is already served by well funded players such as EvenUp and Supio and by record retrieval vendors, and that the 'unified data intelligence layer' pitch is broad. Without proof of paying law firms or insurers and a clear wedge, partners may prefer a narrower product.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Seed at 1.15x the 59 percent anchor: vertical legal AI with a 5 person team and hot category. Above anchor because the market attracted investors, but wide uncertainty.

bands.rationale: Small pre-seed of about 600K to 1.5M on a SAFE, barely above the YC deal. If law firm pilots are slow, a small pre-seed follows.
Typical 2026 seed near the 3.0M US median deal size and 18M pre money from PitchBook NVCA via Equidam (see stage_benchmarks.md). Paid pilots with plaintiff firms lead to a seed.
Strong seed led by a known fund, near the YC 2022+ announced median of 4.1M or above. A hot legal AI market gives strong seed interest.
Upside seed or large first round if usage or revenue spikes, common for hot AI categories in 2026. Fast growth in cases processed attracts a larger round.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step above 500K fails if law firm and treatment provider pilots stay unpaid or if investors see EvenUp, Supio and Hona already owning plaintiff workflows. A two sided data layer connecting treatment, records and settlement also needs data partnerships that a five person team may not secure within 12 months.

bands.rationale: Small or bridge style A, or a down-ish A after a slow year. Medlegal workflows are slow to sell.
Median 2022+ YC Series A raise is 14.15M, market 17.4M. Needs 1M plus ARR from firms.
Hot-category A led by a top fund, 62M pre money median market. Needs clear category leadership.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A needs proof of recurring revenue and a data advantage. It fails if the company cannot show settlement outcomes improved or if firms use it as a records add on. Hona reached a 9.5M Series A after reaching over 1M ARR, while Codes Health and InQuery are still stuck at seed or lower, showing how narrow the path is.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B requires expansion beyond plaintiff firms into insurers or providers and a defensible data asset. It fails if legal AI incumbents bundle medical workflows and growth stays at the pace of small firm sales cycles. The analogs show that very few medical records and legal companies in this niche, such as Codes Health or InQuery, have gone beyond seed.

bands.rationale: Modest C or growth round, or venture debt plus equity. Few reach this step.
Typical C or later; 2022+ YC median C is 45M, D plus 97.5M. Needs multiple lines.
Breakout later round at multi billion value. Needs dominance.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C or later needs a regulated data platform operating at national scale with several revenue lines. It fails if medical data access, HIPAA friction and bundling by category leaders such as EvenUp limit expansion, and the company ends as a mid sized tool or an acquisition target for a legal software vendor, as RiskAngle ended.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Failure is most likely a niche where law firms buy a cheaper records tool and bigger legal AI vendors add medical chronology, leaving the company with small contracts. RiskAngle and PatientBank show records startups end in acquihires or shutdown. Success needs proof that settlement speed data is unique.

technical_complexity.rationale: Extracting and linking medical records, billing and legal data needs OCR, language models and integrations with providers. A five person team can build intake and summaries in three months, but a unified data layer across treatment and settlement depends on partnerships and access.

takeover_risk.rationale: Legal AI leaders have distribution among plaintiff firms and can add medical treatment tracking within months. The moat is proprietary provider data and settlement outcomes.

evidence.claim: Plaintiff firms pay for AI case work today, shown by EvenUp and Supio products and pricing.
Medical record review is a paid service sold to insurers and law firms.

roadmap.goal: Show paying plaintiff firms and a measurable settlement time gain.
Show recurring revenue from firms and early provider partnerships.

pros.point: Defined paying buyer with a large per case value
pros.evidence: Plaintiff firms already buy AI tools and pay per case.

pros.point: Five person team is larger than the typical YC start
pros.evidence: More capacity to ship integrations and sell.

weaknesses: Says nothing about medical or legal
brand.rationale: Wayco is short and neutral and could stretch past medlegal. Past YC names like Hona show a short invented name can work in personal injury software. The name has little effect either way.

narrative.headline: Vertical medlegal AI in a hot, funded category; seed is likely, Series A depends on beating EvenUp class rivals on data.
narrative.general_summary: Wayco builds a data layer for the medical side of legal cases, from intake to settlement. Plaintiff firms already pay for AI tools, legal AI has drawn large funding, and YC analogs like Hona reached a Series A, so a seed above the YC deal is more likely than not. The risk is crowding by EvenUp and Supio and the difficulty of getting medical data. The ladder sits slightly above the B2B cohort anchors at seed and A because the category is investor friendly, with wide uncertainty.

assumptions: Blind forecast: only the YC listing text for this company was used.
Seed means a round above 500K within about 12 months.
Legal tag cohort too small; B2B cohorts used.
Recorded 2026 batch funding was not used as evidence.
